summary: Defines an XML schema for the vCard data format, so contact information can be represented in XML.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6351 defines xCard, an XML representation of vCard contact information. It specifies how to convert between the two formats and how to handle data that a converter does not recognize.

questions: what is the difference between vcard and xcard
how to convert vcard to xml
subtitle: Represent vCard contact data as XML with a defined mapping back to the original format.

tldr.problem: Some systems already have XML tools but would otherwise need a separate parser for vCard contact data.
tldr.mechanism: xCard maps vCard properties, parameters, and values to XML elements using a RELAX NG schema.
tldr.outcome: The mapping preserves the vCard data model and defines how converters handle extensions and unknown values. RFC 6351 is updated by RFC 6868.

today: RFC 6351 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2011. The unit metadata says RFC 6868 updates it and lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: The Purpose of xCard
sections.content:
vCard is a text-based format for representing and exchanging information about people and other entities. RFC 6351 defines xCard, an XML representation of the same data structure.

The mapping is one-to-one, so systems with an XML engine can reuse it instead of writing a separate vCard parser. The schema is expressed in RELAX NG and appears in the appendix.
sections.plainLanguage: xCard stores the same contact information as vCard, but uses XML elements. A program that already processes XML can use that format for contact cards.

sections.title: Mapping Properties and Parameters
sections.content:
vCard properties, parameters, and value types map to XML elements. For example, the vCard FN property maps to an fn element containing a text value. Parameters appear inside a parameters element within the property.

A list-valued parameter is represented by repeated XML elements. Structured properties, such as the vCard name property, become nested elements for parts such as surname and given name. The required root is vcards, even when the document contains only one vcard. Conversion to and from vCard occurs after unfolding or before folding lines, respectively.
sections.plainLanguage: Each vCard field becomes a named XML element, and parameters are placed inside that field. A document uses a vcards root even when it contains one card.

sections.title: A Card in XML
sections.content:
The RFC's example represents a complete contact card under a vcards root. It includes a formatted name, structured name, birthday, anniversary, languages, organization, address, telephone numbers, email, location, key, time zone, and URL.

A smaller example shows a TYPE parameter on a telephone property. Its type element contains separate text values such as voice and video, while the telephone URI appears in a uri element.
sections.plainLanguage: The example puts common contact details into separate XML fields. A telephone field can have several type labels, each represented as its own value.

sections.title: Extensions and Unknown Elements
sections.content:
New vCard properties, parameters, data types, and values are expected to define corresponding xCard extensions. New XML property and parameter names MUST be lowercase so conversion back to vCard works consistently.

Unregistered vCard extensions beginning with X- or VND- use XML element names beginning with x- or vnd-. A parser MUST ignore XML elements and attributes whose expanded names it does not recognize. The schema does not check property counts, so the cardinality rules from RFC 6350 still apply.
sections.plainLanguage: Extensions need matching names in the XML format. A parser skips unfamiliar XML fields, while card producers still follow the property-count rules in RFC 6350.

sections.title: Converting Between the Formats
sections.content:
A converter must preserve values it does not recognize. When converting vCard to xCard, an unknown property type or parameter can be represented with an unknown element containing its original text. Names become lowercase, and vCard escaping and parameter quoting are undone.

When converting xCard to vCard, recognized properties use their vCard representation. Unrecognized elements or attributes nested inside a standard property may be dropped, so the RFC recommends keeping extensions at the property level. Names become uppercase, and escaping and quoting are applied for vCard output.
sections.plainLanguage: Converters keep unfamiliar values in a form they can carry between formats. Extra data nested inside a standard XML property may be lost when converting back, so extensions should be placed at the property level.

sections.title: Security and Registered Format Details
sections.content:
The security considerations for plain vCard also apply to xCard. The RFC notes that XML Signature and XML Encryption can provide authentication and confidentiality.

IANA registered the XML namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:vcard-4.0 and the media type application/vcard+xml. The registration recommends using the utf-8 character set.
sections.plainLanguage: xCard has the same security concerns as vCard. XML tools can sign data to identify its source or encrypt it to restrict who can read it.
